note: Manière is the noun manner/way. The current bare gloss 'somewhat/kinda/a bit' belongs to constructions such as de manière rather than being a straightforward noun meaning.
Coin should foreground corner/area/spot and also means wedge. 'Quack' is an onomatopoeic/specialized use and should not lead the entry.
The entry omits the basic noun entirely: bois = wood/woods. The same spelling is also a very common form of boire meaning 'drink/you drink'.
proposed_english: wood; woods; drink!; I/you drink (forms of boire, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Camp means camp and can also mean side/faction/group; the current camping-ground-only gloss is too narrow.
Paraître is primarily the verb appear/seem/be published; 'appearance' is the noun le paraître and requires noun POS if retained.
proposed_english: to appear; to seem; to be published; appearance (le paraître, noun use)

note: Armée is the noun army but also the feminine past-participle/adjectival form 'armed'. The common homographic reading is missing.
Information is not merely 'an item of information'; it is the general noun information and can also mean news/inquiry/investigation in context.
proposed_english: information; piece of information; news; inquiry/investigation (context-dependent)

note: Professeur means teacher as well as professor; limiting it to professor would mislead learners in ordinary school contexts.
Fond also commonly means background, depth, bottom/core, and substance; the current back/base/bottom gloss is incomplete.
proposed_english: bottom; back; background; depth; base; core/substance

note: Régler very commonly means pay/settle a bill or matter, in addition to regulate/set/adjust. This everyday use is missing.
proposed_english: to adjust; to set; to regulate; to pay; to settle; to resolve

note: Meal names vary regionally. In contemporary France déjeuner is lunch; in Belgium/Switzerland and some other varieties it can mean breakfast. The current unqualified dual gloss can confuse learners.
proposed_english: lunch; to have lunch (standard France); breakfast/to have breakfast in some regional varieties
to direct; to lead; to manage/run; to aim; to steer; to direct (a film)

note: Compris is principally the past participle of comprendre ('understood') and can function adjectivally as included/understood. POS should explicitly include past participle.
Ravir very commonly means delight/thrill/enchant. The current entry lists only older/violent senses such as abduct/plunder and omits the everyday modern meaning.
proposed_english: to delight; to thrill; to enchant; to abduct/carry off (older/formal)

note: Marché is the noun market/deal/contract and also the past participle of marcher ('walked/worked' depending context). The entry mentions the participle but labels only noun.
proposed_english: market; deal; contract; walked/worked (past participle of marcher, context-dependent)

note: Visite is not only the noun visit; it is also a common finite/imperative form of visiter ('visits; visit!').
proposed_english: visit; visits; visit! (forms of visiter, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Poste has several basic senses beyond job/post office: post/position/station and device/set in compounds. The current gloss is too narrow.
proposed_english: post; position; job; station; post office; set/device (context-dependent)

note: Forme is the noun form/shape and also a common finite/imperative form of former ('forms/shapes; form!').
proposed_english: form; shape; forms/shapes; form! (forms of former, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Dame is lady/queen and has a dated interjection use ('indeed!/well!'). Since interjection POS is listed, that meaning should be represented or POS removed.
